package.description: Desktop Jabber/XMPP client based on Converse.js and Electron

en-US.description: Desktop Jabber/XMPP client based on Converse.js and Electron
en-US.name: Converse Desktop
en-US.releaseNotes:
- Update Electron to v45.0.0 (includes the fix for the leaked eMudhra CA keys)
- Update Converse.js to v14.0.1
Verifying your download
SHA256SUMS lists the SHA-256 checksum of every package in this release, and SHA256SUMS.asc is a GPG signature of that file by JC Brand, using the key with this fingerprint:
F5B0 650F F304 9B8D 0EA3  E66C A03B 84D8 866F FEA4
Download SHA256SUMS, SHA256SUMS.asc and your package into the same folder, then:
1. Import the key and check its fingerprint matches the one above:
   gpg --keyserver hkps://keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys F5B0650FF3049B8D0EA3E66CA03B84D8866FFEA4
2. Check the signature. The output should say Good signature from "JC Brand":
   gpg --verify SHA256SUMS.asc SHA256SUMS
3. Check your package against the list. The output should say OK for the file you downloaded:
   - Linux: sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
   - macOS: shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS
   - Windows (PowerShell): run Get-FileHash "Converse.Desktop.Setup.14.0.1.exe" and compare the hash with the line for that file in SHA256SUMS.
The Windows and macOS packages are not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper will warn you when you open them. Checking the signature as described above confirms that the package is the one we published.
